# text_minilm_v2 — StockNet, time-ordered split (generated by `eval/report.py` from `text_minilm_v2.json`)

Train 2014-01-02→2014-12-31 (21,480 ticker-days) · calibration 2015-01-02→2015-06-30 (10,788) · test 2015-07-01→2016-03-31 (16,443) · 87 tickers · α = 0.1 (target coverage 90%) · seed 0 · text scorer: MiniLM-L6 + LR (TFNS) · y = next-day close-to-close log return in %, forecast issued after the 16:00 ET close (widths in percentage points) · runtime 217.4 s.

Reproduce: `bash eval/fetch_data.sh && PYTHONPATH=. nice -n 10 .venv/bin/python eval/prepare.py --scorer minilm && PYTHONPATH=. nice -n 10 .venv/bin/python eval/run_baselines.py --tag text_minilm_v2 --scorer minilm`

## Ablation × conformal method (clean test data)

`cqr_aci` is our own ACI loop (Gibbs & Candès 2021) on CQR scores; split and CQR are MAPIE 1.5. Mean daily coverage has a 90% day-block bootstrap CI (date-cluster inference); pooled Kupiec/Christoffersen p-values ignore same-day correlation.

| Model | Method | Coverage | Mean daily cov. [90% CI] | Mean width | Winkler | Kupiec p | Christoffersen p | Cov. high-vol | Cov. 5+ tweets |

| price_only | cqr_mapie | 86.8% | 86.8% [84.9%, 88.7%] | 4.774 | 7.543 | 2.32e-38 | 0.000969 | 85.5% | 87.1% |

| text_only | cqr_mapie | 82.8% | 82.8% [80.0%, 85.4%] | 4.292 | 8.625 | 8.89e-175 | 8.61e-59 | 78.2% | 83.7% |

## Attacks (budget k = 3 injected documents per ticker-day; every test ticker-day attacked unless stated)

Pump: 3 posts with the template's sentiment from the deployed scorer (0.952) and the trust our scorer gives a fresh, unverified, zero-follower account (0.101). Median forecast shift +0.0943 pp (95th pct |shift| 0.1956 pp).

| Scenario | Method | Coverage | Mean width | Certified ⊇ clean-covered rows? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | CQR | 86.7% | 4.756 | — |
| pump | CQR | 86.4% | 4.721 | — |
| pump | certified CQR | 89.4% | 5.185 | yes |
| oracle: worst of 53 variants per row (knows y) | CQR | 84.7% | — | — |
| worst fixed variant #1: sents [1.0, 1.0, 1.0], trusts [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] | CQR / certified | 85.7% / 89.5% | 4.634 / 5.195 | yes |
| worst fixed variant #2: sents [1.0, 1.0], trusts [1.0, 1.0] | CQR / certified | 85.8% / 89.9% | 4.637 / 5.281 | yes |
| worst fixed variant #3: sents [1.0], trusts [1.0] | CQR / certified | 85.8% / 90.1% | 4.644 / 5.314 | yes |

**Guaranteed floor (fixed offset, real arithmetic plus a derived round-off margin):** for every attack within the budget, the certified symmetric-CQR interval covers every row that the clean symmetric-CQR interval covers, so certified coverage under attack ≥ 86.7% on this test set (retrospective, not a future coverage probability). The 53-variant oracle against plain CQR is a finite score-space search, not a worst-case bound.

Beyond the certified budget (k = 3 certificate, more posts injected; no guarantee applies):

| Posts injected | Plain CQR coverage | Certified (k = 3) coverage | Certified width | Still ⊇ clean-covered rows? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 85.7% | 87.0% | 4.800 | no |
| 6 | 85.8% | 86.6% | 4.760 | no |
| 10 | 86.2% | 86.9% | 4.787 | no |

## CR-ACI (certified box + our ACI loop, γ = 0.01)

Per-row containment holds only at a shared offset (the fixed-offset table above). CR-ACI's clean and attacked runs adapt their offsets separately and need not be nested (counterexample in `tests/test_review_fixes.py`); ACI's guarantee is long-run *mean daily* miscoverage, with worst-case bound (max(α, 1−α) + γ)/(γT) — weak at this horizon.

| Run | Coverage | Mean daily cov. [90% CI] | Mean width | Cov. on attacked days | ACI α_t range | days α_t ≤ 0 / ≥ 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cqr_aci_clean | 89.5% | 89.5% [87.5%, 91.2%] | 5.220 | — | [0.076, 0.104] | 0 / 0 |
| cqr_aci_pump | 89.4% | 89.4% [87.4%, 91.1%] | 5.229 | — | [0.074, 0.103] | 0 / 0 |
| cr_aci_clean | 89.5% | 89.5% [87.6%, 91.1%] | 5.243 | — | [0.076, 0.103] | 0 / 0 |
| cr_aci_pump | 89.7% | 89.7% [87.8%, 91.4%] | 5.283 | — | [0.081, 0.107] | 0 / 0 |
| cqr_aci_burst_worst | 89.5% | 89.5% [87.6%, 91.2%] | 5.209 | 89.5% | [0.076, 0.103] | 0 / 0 |
| cr_aci_burst_worst | 89.6% | 89.6% [87.7%, 91.2%] | 5.251 | 90.7% | [0.078, 0.104] | 0 / 0 |

Burst runs attack only three pre-specified 10-day windows (test days 20–29, 80–89, 140–149) with the worst fixed variant from the oracle grid; coverage on attacked days is what an attacker who concentrates on the days they trade would face.

## Soundness checks of the certificate

- Degenerate box reproduces the model exactly: max |error| = 0.00e+00
- Certificate's feature recomputation matches the aggregator: max |error| = 1.11e-16
- Clean features lie inside the box computed from attacked documents: 100.00% of test rows
- Own symmetric CQR vs MAPIE `symmetric_correction=True`: max |diff| = 0.00e+00
- Unit tests (`tests/`): deletion box sound and exact vs brute force; tree bounds sound; trust deletion- and injection-stable; ACI long-run bound |mean err − α| ≤ (max(α, 1−α) + γ)/(γT) on adversarial sequences; ACI boundary cases (whole line / empty set).

## Caveats
- One seed and one fixed 87-stock universe (StockNet; survivorship). VADER scorer unless stated.
- Adjusted closes are back-adjusted for dividends and splits; we use only return ratios, so levels do not leak, but volume is not split-adjusted.
- The certificate assumes clean calibration data and covers injection of up to k documents; edits of real documents and price manipulation are out of scope.
- Empty intervals: 0.0% of fusion ACI rows (empty sets count as misses; width/Winkler exclude them).
- This test period has been looked at several times during development; the untouched-data text-utility test is `eval/results/text_utility_djia_v1.json` (pre-registered).
